text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz says compulsory eight-year education will be put into practice in stages and will become effective in the whole of Turkey by next year.
- Anti-Islamist government plans to encourage exporters to reach a target of $50 billion in exports in five years.
MILLIYET
- President Suleyman Demirel criticises leaders of the previous Islamist-led coalition for creating social tension.
- Yilmaz vows to merge separate military and civilian intelligence units.
HURRIYET
- Deputy Prime Minister Bulent Ecevit says the customs union with the European Union is to the disadvantage of Turkey and asks the foreign ministry to start reviewing it.
- Forest fire kills two and destroys 600 hectars of pine tree near the famous southern holiday resort Antalya.
YENI YUZYIL
- State minister responsible for economy says he will appear on private television stations if he is paid $5,000 which he will spend on youth sports activities in south and southeast Turkey.
- Celebrities Elizabeth Taylor, Julio Iglesias and Shirley Bassey will come to Istanbul on July 19 for a charity night to raise money for Chechen children.
RADIKAL
- The new government will face difficulty in realising its $4 billion revenue target from privatisation considering Turkey has raised only $3.1 billion from privatisation in the past ten years.
CUMHURIYET
- The cabinet reaches an agreement on a partial amnesty for jailed journalists.
DUNYA
- Energy ministry plans to solve Turkey's problem of not being able to stock natural gas by building underground warehouses in western Turkey.
ZAMAN
- Professor Guven Onay, chairman of association to develop national mines, says Turkey is a poor guardian of its rich mines worth of $2 trillion as it does not yet have the modern technology.
